saints.name: Sts. Philip and James
saints.title: Apostles
saints.shortBlurb: Two of the Twelve, joined in a single feast because their relics were together enshrined at Rome…
biography: Philip was a native of Bethsaida in Galilee, the town of Peter and Andrew. Called directly by the Lord, he at once brought Nathanael to Him; it was Philip who reckoned the cost of feeding the five thousand, whom the Greeks approached wishing to see Jesus, and who prayed, 'Lord, show us the Father'.

After Pentecost, tradition sends Philip to Phrygia, where he was crucified at Hierapolis under Domitian. James, the son of Alphaeus, called the Less, governed the church of Jerusalem as its first bishop and wrote the Epistle that bears his name; about the year 62 he was thrown from the pinnacle of the Temple and clubbed to death as he prayed for his murderers.

The relics of the two apostles have rested together in the Roman basilica of the Holy Apostles since the sixth century, whence they share a single feast. Long kept on 1 May, the day of that basilica's dedication, it was moved in 1969 to 3 May, the first of May being given to St. Joseph the Worker.
saints.knownFor: Their apostolic witness to Christ, sealed in martyrdom.
